correctness.rationale: For each overlap size, independence gives the exact joint probability and marginal products, including same-set mutually exclusive cases. The finite covariance has a positive prefactor times a strictly decreasing F with opposite endpoint signs. Bernoulli inequality bounds root; n=r+1 isolates two overlaps; fixed-r expansion via A3/A2 yields stated n^-1 term. A standalone verifier independently enumerated all edge states for five (n,r) pairs and exact probabilities plus 12,047 finite tests; enumeration is corroborative.

None of these accessible portions settles the strict single-crossing theorem for every motif order or its 1/n correction; full general papers unavailable and are recorded as residual risk.

value.rationale: The count covariance of dense graphlets in the simplest random-graph null law is a natural mathematical dependence invariant, unlike an arbitrary finite table. A universal sign reversal and sharp location for all motif orders explain when a nearly complete induced subgraph count agrees/disagrees with actual clique abundance; this is relevant to joint motif feature normalization. The contribution is the structural root theorem and asymptotic rather than basic moment enumeration.
